Subject: Control mapping + operator info for EU pilot

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we scope our pilot in FRA (EU) we need a short, consumable artifact that maps CAIQ / SIG controls to the actual evidence we can reference from Redwood for a private (VPC) deployment. Specifically Medline needs:

- A one-page mapping (control -> exhibit / file) for the CAIQ questions we flagged during the SOC2 pre-check.
- The expected operator roster (roles + minimal contact info) who would have access to the FRA tenant for onboarding.
- A compact VPC runbook for peering and emergency fallback (what we hand to our network team).

Timeline is tight: pilot kickoff Feb 9, so procurement/security needs these by Jan 22.

If you can attach a zipped example or pointing link that would be great. We also have a short SIG spreadsheet I'll share if you need context.

Appreciate it —
Lena

Hi Lena —

Thanks for the clear ask. I've attached an initial CAIQ->evidence mapping for EU-hosted private deployments (redwood_caiaq_mapping_eu_v1.xlsx) and a topology sketch for the Frankfurt privatelink (privatelink_topology_fra.png). These are intentionally concise so your security and network teams can triage quickly.

Quick notes (summary):
- Most CAIQ controls we map to SOC 2 exhibits (we include SOC 2 exhibit IDs in the sheet), plus a handful tied to our keystore/HSM partitioning for EU nodes.
- Operator roster is redacted in the attached sample (we provide a sanitized CSV with roles & escalation lines; full roster is shared under NDA/secure transfer).
- The runbook is a short-form operational playbook inside the sheet (steps for peering, expected handshake times, fallback to hosted region). We can expand into a full runbook if your teams prefer.

Next steps:
1) I can share the full operator roster over a secure share once we have an inbound-contact email for your procurement/security team (or via your SFTP).
2) Rishi will add a note on KMS/HSM partitioning and operator separation to the mapping later today.
3) Marissa will follow up on procurement timing and the MSA / DocuSign link.

Hi Lena / Olga,

Adding a couple of security-specific clarifications to the mapping Olga shared:

- KMS partitioning: EU tenant keys are stored in an EU-only keyring backed by HSMs in the FRA region. CAIQ control mappings pointing to key custody reference Exhibit SOC2-KMS-2025. We do not replicate signing keys outside the designated region unless explicitly authorized.
- Operator access: We enforce Just-In-Time operator access for critical infra operations; operators get ephemeral RBAC tokens tied to audits. The attached operator_roster_sample.csv is a sanitized example of roles + escalation contacts. Full operator identity proofs require an executed DPA + access request.
- Audit logs & retention: Tenant-level audit trails for operator actions are retained for 1 year by default for private deployments; retention extension options available as an add-on.

If Medline needs an HSM attestation snippet (FIPS level + vendor) I can pull the short-form artifact and include it in the evidence pack.

Rishi

Appreciate the fast turnaround. The mapping and topology look helpful at first pass. A couple of asks before we close the pack for our board:

- We will receive the sanitized operator roster via SFTP — please send the SFTP endpoint and an ingress contact.

If you can push the HSM snippet and the runbook draft by Friday Jan 23 I'll route to procurement/security for final signoff. I can accept a Google Drive link (internal secure folder) for the artifacts.
